verifications.claim: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact date.

verifications.claim: The Challenger orbiter disintegrated 73 seconds after liftoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'broke apart 73 seconds into its flight'; R2: 'exploded 73 seconds after liftoff'; R3: 'disintegrated 73 seconds after launch'

verifications.claim: The disaster killed all seven crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'killing all seven crew members'; R2: 'killing all seven crew members'; R3: 'killing all seven astronauts'

verifications.claim: A failed O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster, compromised by cold temperatures, caused the fatal structural failure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'failure of the primary and secondary O-ring seals in a joint in the right Space Shuttle Solid Rocket Booster (SRB). The record-low temperatures'; R2: 'O-ring seal failure in a rocket booster, which was worsened by cold weather'; R3: 'O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster (SRB) failed... hardened the O-rings'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on cause, location, and cold temperature factor.

verifications.claim: The disaster forced a 32-month shutdown of the shuttle program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The disaster resulted in a 32-month hiatus in the Space Shuttle program.'

verifications.claim: The shuttle broke up 73 seconds into flight at 11:38 a.m. EST.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launched... at 11:38:00 a.m.... disintegrated... at 16:39:13 UTC (11:39:13 a.m. EST'; R3: 'launched at 11.38 a.m. EST... disintegrated 73 seconds'
verifications.reasoning: Launch at 11:38 a.m. EST, breakup at 11:39:13 a.m. EST (73s later); claim incorrectly attributes breakup time as 11:38.

verifications.claim: The shuttle broke up 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'disintegrated about 46,000 feet (14 km) above the Atlantic Ocean'

verifications.claim: A cold-induced failure of the O-ring seal allowed hot gas to breach the solid rocket booster.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The record-low temperatures... stiffened the rubber O-rings... hot pressurized gas from within the SRB leaked'; R3: 'hardened the O-rings... ‘blow by’ both the primary and secondary O-rings'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm cold effect leading to hot gas breach.

verifications.claim: The breach of the solid rocket booster led to the rupture of the external fuel tank.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'leaked through the joint and burned through... into the tank itself. The collapse of the ET's internal structures'

verifications.claim: The seven crew members were Dick Scobee, Michael J. Smith, Ronald McNair, Ellison Onizuka, Judy Resnik, Greg Jarvis, and Christa McAuliffe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Dick Scobee... Michael J. Smith... Ronald McNair... Ellison Onizuka... Judith Resnik... Gregory Jarvis... Christa McAuliffe'; R2 and R6 match names (minor spelling variants like Judy/Judith, Greg/Gregory)

verifications.claim: All seven crew members lost their lives.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'killing all seven crew members'; R2: 'killing all seven crew members'

verifications.claim: Michael J. Smith was the pilot.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Michael J. Smith, pilot'; R2: 'pilot Michael J. Smith'

verifications.claim: Dick Scobee was the Commander.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Dick Scobee, commander'; R2: 'Francis R. Scobee, the mission commander'

verifications.claim: The last known words from the crew came from pilot Michael J. Smith, who said "Uh oh."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pilot Mike Smith said "Uh-oh", which was the last crew comment recorded.'

verifications.claim: A comment from Commander Dick Scobee followed, which was cut off.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate Smith's 'Uh-oh' as last crew comment; Scobee's prior comment at T+68, no post-'Uh-oh' comment mentioned.

verifications.claim: The crew cabin was found in the ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crew compartment containing human remains... were recovered from the ocean floor'

verifications.claim: The astronauts died from the massive impact (over 200 mph) of the cabin with the ocean, rather than the initial explosion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'impact... at 207 mph (333 km/h)... too violent to be survivable'; 'several crew members are thought to have survived the initial breakup'; 'forces... probably insufficient to cause major injury'
verifications.reasoning: Speed and cause of death precisely match.

verifications.claim: The Rogers Commission identified the technical cause as the O-ring failure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the Rogers Commission... commission determined that the cause... hot gas blowing past the O-rings'

verifications.claim: The Rogers Commission highlighted that NASA management ignored engineer warnings regarding the cold weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA managers also disregarded engineers' warnings about the dangers of launching in low temperatures'

verifications.claim: Christa McAuliffe was the "teacher in space."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'taking schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe into space under the Teacher in Space Project'; R2: 'first teacher in space'

verifications.claim: Christa McAuliffe's lessons were performed in space in 2018.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention any 2018 lessons; project was cancelled post-disaster.

verifications.claim: A large segment of the Challenger was discovered on the ocean floor in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On November 10, 2022, NASA announced that a 20-foot (6 m) piece of the shuttle had been found... off the coast of Florida.'

verifications.claim: There is an upcoming limited series about the Challenger mission starring Kristen Stewart as Sally Ride, which is in development.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Kristen Stewart’s ‘The Challenger’ Series Lands Greenlight... play astronaut... Sally Ride'; R5: 'Kristen Stewart will play Sally Ride... Amazon finally greenlights mini-series ‘The Challenger’'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm series titled 'The Challenger' starring Stewart as Ride, greenlit (recently upcoming); covers Challenger events though Ride not on mission.
